claims: On July 20, 1969, American astronaut Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon during NASA's Apollo 11 mission.
Neil Armstrong stepped onto the lunar surface at 10:56 p.m. EDT.
Neil Armstrong declared, "That's one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind".
Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin explored the lunar surface for over two hours.
Michael Collins orbited above while Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin explored the lunar surface.
Apollo 11 was commanded by Neil Armstrong.
Buzz Aldrin was the Lunar Module Pilot of Apollo 11.
Michael Collins was the Command Module Pilot of Apollo 11.
The Lunar Module Eagle landed at the Sea of Tranquility on July 20, 1969.
The Lunar Module Eagle landed at 4:17 p.m. EDT (20:17 UTC).
The Lunar Module Eagle landed with only seconds of fuel remaining.
Neil Armstrong took manual control to avoid a crater.
Neil Armstrong piloted the craft over hazardous terrain.
The astronauts spent roughly 212 hours walking on the lunar surface.
The astronauts took photographs on the lunar surface.
The astronauts collected samples on the lunar surface.
The astronauts planted a U.S. flag on the lunar surface.
The Apollo 11 team returned safely to Earth on July 24, 1969.
Armstrong and Aldrin’s walk was broadcast to millions.
